purpose: Make the framework's progressive build explicit. Each layer introduces atoms and becomes able to express something the layers below cannot. A layer may depend only on layers beneath it.
provenance: NOT a new taxonomy. The ladder is read off docs/FORMAL_SYSTEM_SPECIFICATION.md, whose 14 sections are already ordered by dependency (charts -> transitions -> gluing -> authority -> verification -> reachability -> saturation -> method acquisition -> assimilation). The papers were carved by THEME on top of a spec already ordered by DEPENDENCY, which is why they do not build on each other.

measured_paper_coupling.note: Cross-paper references, self excluded, measured 2026-08-14 over all .tex.
measured_paper_coupling.finding: Hub-and-spoke, not a chain. IV and VI reference all five others; I, II, III have exactly one cross-reference each and V has none. Paper II contains ZERO references to Paper I by any phrasing, though it sits directly above it on the ladder.

layers.name: Objects, facets, projections, contexts
layers.expresses: That two sources describe the same object through different projection operators under different contexts. Without this layer, disagreement cannot be distinguished from difference-of-view.
layers.benefit_obligation: Does context-aligned projection reduce false contradiction rate versus naive text comparison? Observable: FCR from the quantitative evaluation model.

layers.name: Typed transitions and relation algebra
layers.expresses: That a step from one object to another has a type, and that composing steps is licensed or not. Without it, any two claims can be chained.
layers.benefit_obligation: Does typed composition prevent unsupported chains a untyped baseline admits? Observable: unsupported-composition rate.

layers.name: Context alignment, contradiction and gluing
layers.expresses: That locally consistent pieces may have no global section. This is the layer where obstructions become first-class, and Paper I's three-context parity construction lives here.
layers.benefit_obligation: Does retaining obstructions prevent wrong gluings that a pairwise-only representation admits? This is exactly Proposition prop:obstruction-blind, and it is currently proved but not measured.

layers.name: Scientific authority as a partial order
layers.expresses: That a claim's evidential standing is multi-coordinate and that only certified transitions may change it. Without it, fluency substitutes for evidence.
layers.benefit_obligation: Does the authority boundary reduce unsupported authority upgrades versus an ungoverned arm? Observable: ALR. NOT YET MEASURED - see mechanism_benefit_ledger.

layers.name: Goal-conditioned reachability and support structure
layers.expresses: That solving is search for an authority-valid support structure reaching the target, and that FAILING is informative: the min-cost cut names what would have to be established. This is the framework's verb.
layers.benefit_obligation: Does navigating a distilled support structure solve more than reading raw sources at matched total budget? This is arm C of the benefit experiment and the load-bearing open question.
layers.defect_note: This layer had NO paper home until 2026-08-14. Its specification sat in a doc marked research-only, and its three appearances in the papers were all CONSTRAINING (Paper I's is inside a noninterference section). The framework's central verb was present only where it was being restrained.

layers.name: Bounded epistemic saturation
layers.expresses: When search may stop. Requires L4 because saturation is relative to a declared route family, and requires a finite basis to be certifiable rather than merely bounded.
layers.benefit_obligation: Does stopping on this rule beat stopping arbitrarily at matched budget? External observable available: set-completeness IoU. NOT YET MEASURED.

layers.name: Experience, challenge learning and method acquisition
layers.expresses: That the method itself is an object the system can revise. Requires L5: you cannot tell whether a method change helped until you can say when search was done.
layers.benefit_obligation: Fresh-task lift versus a static-method parent. Currently BLOCKED_ON_CAPABILITY_QUALIFICATION, explicitly not a null.

layers.name: External method assimilation and constructive invention
layers.expresses: That a competitor's mechanism can be absorbed under RAKL conditions. Requires L6: assimilation is a method change, so it inherits the method-evolution gate.
layers.benefit_obligation: Measured transfer under RAKL conditions, not feature parity. One instance now exists: MEC-DERIVATION_QUANTIFIED_REFUSAL transferred in adapted form; the faithful import was refuted by measurement.

ladder_violations_in_current_carve.violation: Paper II covers L1-TRANSITION and L2-GLUING, both of which depend on L0-OBJECT which Paper I owns - yet Paper II contains zero references to Paper I.
ladder_violations_in_current_carve.consequence: The dependency is real but invisible. A reader of Paper II cannot see what it is built on, and Paper I's results are not available to justify Paper II's constructions.

ladder_violations_in_current_carve.violation: L4-NAVIGATION had no paper home until PR #623, despite being specified in FORMAL_SYSTEM_SPECIFICATION.md section 8.
ladder_violations_in_current_carve.consequence: The framework's central verb was unclaimed. Papers are carved by mechanism TYPE (nouns); the loop is a VERB, so it had nowhere to land.

ladder_violations_in_current_carve.violation: Papers IV and VI reference all five others while I, II, III, V reference at most one each.
ladder_violations_in_current_carve.consequence: Composition happens only in IV and VI - which are precisely the two papers reporting REFUTED and COST_ONLY benefit. The papers that never compose report success about their own layer in isolation.

open_residuals.statement: The layer-to-paper mapping is authored from section headings and cross-reference counts, not from a claim-by-claim audit.
open_residuals.closure_action: Map every theorem-like claim in each paper to a layer, and flag any claim that uses an atom from a higher layer.

open_residuals.statement: Six of eight layers have an unmeasured benefit obligation.
open_residuals.closure_action: Each layer's obligation names an observable; execute them in ladder order, since a higher layer's benefit is not interpretable if a lower one is unmeasured.
